budget.delta: Installing this adds {tokens, number} always-on tokens and {tools, number} always-visible tools.
budget.deltaNone: This package adds no always-visible surface.
budget.deltaSpawns: It can also start extra paid model contexts.
budget.description: What your installed packages cost on every single request, before you use any of them.
budget.empty: Nothing installed, so nothing is being paid for.
budget.spawningHint: One subagent task is a fresh paid context, so this dominates cost far more than schema size. It is counted separately rather than folded into a token total that would understate it.
budget.title: Context budget
budget.unknown: {count, plural, =1 {1 package unmeasured} other {# packages unmeasured}}
budget.unknownHint: These are not in the reviewed catalog. Their cost is unknown, which is not the same as zero.

aliou-pi-guardrails.removeWhen: Remove when you switch to Permission Modes or the Gotgenes policy stack — never run two policy layers at once.
aliou-pi-guardrails.risk: A full-authority extension: prompts are advice, not containment. There is no OS sandbox behind them.
aliou-pi-guardrails.summary: Deterministic prompts for protected files, out-of-workspace access and dangerous commands. Four extension entry points, no model tool, no prompt injection.

gotgenes-pi-permission-system.removeWhen: Remove if you go back to Guardrails or Permission Modes — these three are mutually exclusive.
gotgenes-pi-permission-system.risk: Still not an OS sandbox. Forwarding approvals from native subagents requires the matching @gotgenes/pi-subagents, not an unrelated subprocess package.
gotgenes-pi-permission-system.summary: Fail-closed allow / ask / deny policy across tools, Bash, paths, MCP, skills, external directories and per-agent overrides. The precise option when policy detail matters more than easy onboarding.

gotgenes-pi-subagents.removeWhen: Remove unless you are running the matching Gotgenes permission system.
gotgenes-pi-subagents.risk: Only coherent as part of the Gotgenes policy stack; on its own it is a subagent package with a narrower feature set than the alternatives.
gotgenes-pi-subagents.summary: In-process subagents with native registration and ask-state forwarding into @gotgenes/pi-permission-system.

juicesharp-rpiv-ask-user-question.removeWhen: Remove if Plan Mode's own plan-only question tool is enough for how you work.
juicesharp-rpiv-ask-user-question.risk: Adds one schema and can interrupt too eagerly. Tune its guidance rather than installing a second question UI.
juicesharp-rpiv-ask-user-question.summary: One structured clarification tool with 2–4 options, previews, notes and free-form answers. No extra model call and no native dependency.

juicesharp-rpiv-todo.removeWhen: Remove only when replacing it — do not run a second todo or task-state extension beside it.
juicesharp-rpiv-todo.risk: Low. It tracks implementation progress, not conversational planning, and confusing the two leads to duplicated state.
juicesharp-rpiv-todo.summary: A visible task overlay whose state survives reload and compaction by replaying session tool calls. No disk state and no API key.

narumitw-pi-chrome-devtools.removeWhen: Cognia already ships agent-browser — remove this unless you specifically need CDP inside Pi.
narumitw-pi-chrome-devtools.risk: Attaching to a personal Chrome profile exposes logged-in pages and cookies. Prefer its isolated temporary profile.
narumitw-pi-chrome-devtools.summary: Lazily exposes native CDP capabilities for navigation, evaluation, screenshots and target selection. Five capability tools once loaded.

narumitw-pi-github-pr.removeWhen: Remove if you read PR state through explicit gh commands instead.
narumitw-pi-github-pr.risk: Repeated process and network calls; account visibility follows your gh auth. It is status only, not a review workflow.
narumitw-pi-github-pr.summary: Passive current-branch PR status through authenticated gh, refreshed periodically and after each turn. No model tool and no comment-body injection.

narumitw-pi-goal.removeWhen: Remove if you also install Workflow — the two duplicate the same lifecycle.
narumitw-pi-goal.risk: Autonomous continuation can compound cost or repeat a bad action, and runtime cost can be very high because it keeps taking turns. Use explicit token budgets and low continuation limits.
narumitw-pi-goal.summary: Session-scoped goals with guarded automatic continuation. Its after-first-goal setting delays the tool surface until a goal exists.

narumitw-pi-lsp.removeWhen: Remove if your gates already give you the same diagnostics faster.
narumitw-pi-lsp.risk: Narrower than a real IDE LSP — no general references or rename workflow. Typecheck, Rust checks and project tests stay authoritative.
narumitw-pi-lsp.summary: Targeted diagnostics and source-fix tools backed by short-lived language servers. Two additional schemas.

narumitw-pi-plan-mode.removeWhen: Remove if you let Permission Modes own planning via its own Plan mode, or if you adopt Workflow.
narumitw-pi-plan-mode.risk: Pi cannot enforce read-only at the sandbox level, so the mode is a convention the model follows rather than a boundary.
narumitw-pi-plan-mode.summary: Conversational read-only planning with an explicit completion handoff and narrow validated Git / gh inspection. Tools and plan text are present only during the workflow.

narumitw-pi-statusline.removeWhen: Remove if you adopt Atelier, which replaces the footer and the completion notification together.
narumitw-pi-statusline.risk: None to the model context. The only hazard is installing a second footer.
narumitw-pi-statusline.summary: Model, thinking level, Git, tools, context, cache, time and cost in the footer. No LLM tool and no injected text, so the model-context cost is negligible.

narumitw-pi-subagents.removeWhen: Remove if you move to pi-subagents or the Gotgenes fork — one delegation implementation only.
narumitw-pi-subagents.risk: Every task starts another paid model context, so token and latency cost can dominate everything else. Working-directory trust is not sandboxing, and the default concurrency and depth are too broad.
narumitw-pi-subagents.summary: Isolated subprocess agents with consultation and auto-routing. Blocking-only exposes four tools; All mode exposes eight.

narumitw-pi-workflow.removeWhen: Defer entirely for now — prefer plan-mode plus goal, which are separately maintained and far more used.
narumitw-pi-workflow.risk: At a much earlier version than the packages it overlaps, and installing it beside plan-mode or goal duplicates state machines.
narumitw-pi-workflow.summary: Combines plan and goal lifecycle in one package. Its own source labels it experimental.

narumitw-pi-worktree.removeWhen: Remove if you never branch through worktrees.
narumitw-pi-worktree.risk: User-driven Git mutation. Note that a worktree is exactly where the Permission Modes sandbox stops containing.
narumitw-pi-worktree.summary: Interactive /worktree session switching. No model tool and no background work, so effectively zero prompt cost.

pi-atelier.removeWhen: Use it instead of statusline plus a notification package, never alongside them.
pi-atelier.risk: Young and broad: it replaces several separate UI packages at once, so a regression affects all of them together.
pi-atelier.summary: A responsive footer and sidebar with context thresholds, session and compaction controls, and completion notification in one package. No model tools.

pi-finish-notification.removeWhen: Remove if you install Atelier, which already supplies notifications. Otherwise review the source first.
pi-finish-notification.risk: Only 102 monthly and 22 weekly downloads, with limited source and maintenance evidence on its package metadata.
pi-finish-notification.summary: A completion notification and nothing else. Tiny footprint and no model context.

pi-mcp-adapter.removeWhen: Keep exactly one adapter. Remove this only if you replace it — never run it alongside pi-codemcp or pi-mcp-tools.
pi-mcp-adapter.risk: MCP servers execute local or remote tools and can receive repository data. Promoted tools cost roughly 150–300 tokens each; the adapter itself warns past 75.
pi-mcp-adapter.summary: Pi's only route to MCP: one lazy proxy tool, a disk metadata cache, reconnect and keepalive, and optional promotion of selected tools to direct schemas.

pi-memory.removeWhen: Remove if Cognia's own long-term memory already covers this; running both means two competing recall paths.
pi-memory.risk: Seven schemas plus recalled content are a meaningful per-turn tax, deep search can take around ten seconds, and stale private facts persist. Project ADRs and AGENTS.md must stay the source of truth.
pi-memory.summary: Seven memory tools over Markdown storage, with stable snapshots and optional qmd semantic indexing.

pi-permission-modes.removeWhen: Remove in a worktree, where its sandbox is no longer containment — keep Guardrails or use whole-process isolation instead.
pi-permission-modes.risk: Only model Bash is OS-sandboxed; file tools are policy-gated and approved escapes run unsandboxed. Worktrees degrade to prompts because the sandbox cannot handle a .git file. Never cycle to YOLO.
pi-permission-modes.summary: Allow / ask / deny with Bash AST gating, macOS sandbox-exec, a network allowlist and tool / skill gating. Injects one sandbox section every turn.

pi-permission-system-legacy.removeWhen: Avoid on Pi 0.84.1. Use @gotgenes/pi-permission-system, and reconsider after a compatible release.
pi-permission-system-legacy.risk: Its npm peer range enumerates Pi versions only through 0.80, not 0.84.1, so it is not declared compatible with the Pi that Cognia verifies against.

pi-rtk-optimizer.removeWhen: Turn compaction off — or remove it — for audits and hard debugging, where the full output is the point.
pi-rtk-optimizer.risk: Compaction can hide evidence and invalidate exact edit anchors. Start in suggestion mode with lossy source filtering off.
pi-rtk-optimizer.summary: Rewrites supported shell commands through the installed rtk binary and compacts noisy Bash, read and grep output.

pi-subagents.removeWhen: Remove if a bounded blocking-only delegation package covers your workload.
pi-subagents.risk: Much broader than the Narumitw package and much easier to over-configure. Its child processes do not natively forward Gotgenes ask prompts, so keep children read-only or give them explicit non-interactive deny policies.
pi-subagents.summary: Rich subprocess delegation with workflows, a fleet UI, MCP selection, schedules and background runs.

pi-web-access.removeWhen: Remove if Cognia's own web tools already cover your retrieval needs.
pi-web-access.risk: Broad outbound network and a wide provider / credential surface. Fetched content, not the schemas, is the real context cost. Keep remote hosted fetchers disabled and never paste keys into JSON.
pi-web-access.summary: Four tools: search, fetch, bounded cached retrieval and claim checking, with GitHub, PDF and video support.

vtstech-pi-long-term-memory.removeWhen: Not recommended at all: prefer pi-memory's explicit retrieval.
vtstech-pi-long-term-memory.risk: Its own package page documents roughly 4K tokens injected on every turn — by far the largest fixed cost in this catalog — against only 191 monthly downloads in the observed snapshot.
vtstech-pi-long-term-memory.summary: Automatic long-term memory injection with three tools.
